title: File:Law Quadrangle, University of Michigan, University Avenue and State Street, Ann Arbor, MI - 54380284362.jpg
author: w_lemay
description: Built in 1924-1933, this group of Collegiate Gothic Revival-style buildings were designed by York and Sawyer and gifted by University of Michigan alumnus William Wilson Cook to house the University of Michigan’s Law School.  The buildings are clad in rough-hewn stone with gabled roofs, bay windows, leaded casement windows, towers at the entrance bays, decorative stone trim, and arched entrance bays.  The buildings are contributing structures in the University of Michigan Central Campus Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978.
modifications: resized; social card cropped with headline
